description.network: Let devices running Cloudflare WARP reach addresses on this Mac's network.
description.route: Send a hostname on your domain to a service on this Mac.
description.review: Review what will change in Cloudflare. Nothing changes until you apply.

network.label: Network
network.help: An address or a range on this Mac's network, like 192.168.1.0/24. Anyone signed in to WARP with your Zero Trust organization can reach it through this Mac.

path.label: Path
path.help: Only requests whose path matches this pattern, e.g. ^/api/. Leave empty for all.

login.label: Who can sign in
login.help: Email addresses, or @domain for everyone there. Visitors get a one-time code by email. Uses Cloudflare Zero Trust (free).

routeSheet.nothingToChange: Nothing to change: it's already set up.

confirm.publicNetwork: Send these public addresses through this Mac

routeSheet.rolledBack: Everything done before the failure was undone. Nothing was left behind.

verify.pending: Checking {url} works… The connector can take a few seconds to connect.
verify.protectedDetail: Cloudflare asks visitors to sign in before they reach your app.

connect.title: Connect
connect.ssh: Visitors connect with cloudflared installed on their computer:
connect.other: Visitors run this on their computer (with cloudflared installed), then keep it open:
connect.sshConfigHint: Or add this to ~/.ssh/config, and plain ssh works:

detail.remote: The service isn't on this Mac

connectCloudflare.title: Connect Cloudflare
connectCloudflare.description: Routes send a hostname on your domain, like app.example.com, to a service on this Mac.

empty.title: No routes yet
empty.noDomains: Add a domain to your Cloudflare account first. Routes use hostnames on your domains.
empty.description: A route sends a hostname like app.example.com to a service on this Mac, such as localhost:3000.

logs.empty: No failed requests. Successful ones aren't logged.

foreign.stopService: It runs as a background service, which may start it again. Whatever it serves stops answering.
foreign.stopProcess: Whatever it serves stops answering. Teitunnel didn't start it, so check nothing else relies on it.
foreign.onlyShown: Teitunnel didn't start this cloudflared, so it only shows it.

tunnels.notOurs: Teitunnel didn't create this tunnel, so it doesn't change its routes. Manage them where it was set up.

running.title: Running
running.linux: Routes stay up after you quit the app and start again when you log in. To keep them up after you log out, run loginctl enable-linger.
running.detail: Routes stay up after you quit the app and start again when you log in.

tunnels.logsEmpty: The connector hasn't logged anything yet.
tunnels.title: Tunnels
tunnels.connectDescription: Tunnels connect this Mac to Cloudflare so your routes can reach it.

empty.title: No tunnels
empty.description: Teitunnel creates a tunnel for this Mac when you add your first route or share a private network.

warning.replacesForeignRecord: {hostname} already has a DNS record ({kind} {content}) that Teitunnel didn't create. It will be replaced.
warning.deletesForeignRecord: The {kind} record for {hostname} ({content}) wasn't created by Teitunnel. It will be deleted.
warning.keepsForeignRecord: The DNS record for {hostname} wasn't created by Teitunnel, so it's left in place.
warning.tunnelEmpty: No routes will be left. The tunnel stays, so adding a route later is quick.
warning.remoteOrigin: {origin} isn't on this Mac. It must be reachable from here.
warning.publicNetwork: {network} isn't a private range. WARP clients would reach those addresses through this Mac instead of the internet.
warning.overlapsNetwork: {network} overlaps {other}, which goes through tunnel “{tunnel}”. For addresses in both, the narrower range wins.

networks.title: Private Networks
networks.noPermission: This account's API token can't read private networks. Give it the Cloudflare Tunnel permission to share them.
networks.empty: Let devices running Cloudflare WARP reach addresses on this Mac's network, like a NAS or a printer.

export.title: Export
export.empty: This Mac has no routes in this account yet, so there's nothing to export.

hint.configYaml: The routes as a cloudflared configuration file, to run them as a locally-managed tunnel or keep as a record.
hint.dockerCompose: A service that runs this tunnel in Docker. The run token isn't included; the file says how to get it.
hint.terraform: Terraform for the Cloudflare provider, with import blocks that adopt the existing tunnel and records instead of recreating them.

import.title: Import from cloudflared
import.description: These routes are in cloudflared config files on this Mac. Imported routes move to this Mac's tunnel; the files are left as they are.

remoteLogs.title: Connector Logs
remoteLogs.description: {address} · cloudflared {version}. Relayed live by Cloudflare while this is open.
remoteLogs.empty: Nothing logged yet. Connection changes and errors appear here as they happen.

traffic.title: Traffic
traffic.emptyHour: Traffic appears here a few seconds after the connector starts.
traffic.emptyHistory: History appears here after the connector has run for a minute.

activity.title: Activity

empty.title: No activity yet
empty.description: Every change Teitunnel makes to Cloudflare is recorded here, step by step.

activity.nothingChanged: Nothing was changed: every step was undone.

startup.title: Startup
startup.footer: Teitunnel opens in the menu bar, without a window. Routes set to keep running don't need this.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.footer: Only when no Teitunnel window is in front. macOS decides how they look in System Settings ▸ Notifications.
notifications.routesDetail: When this Mac's connector loses its connection for more than 20 seconds.
notifications.problemsDetail: When the Doctor finds something new that stops a route working.
notifications.sharesDetail: When a share goes live or stops working.

menuBar.title: Menu bar
menuBar.footer: Closing the window keeps routes and Quick Shares running. Quit Teitunnel with ⌘Q to stop them.
menuBar.showDetail: Status and quick actions without opening the window.

domains.finishSetupDetail: At your registrar, replace the nameservers with these. Changes can take up to a day to be picked up.
domains.title: Domains
domains.connectDescription: Use your own domains, like app.example.com, for services on this Mac.
domains.noneDetail: Add a domain in your Cloudflare dashboard, then refresh.

doctor.title: Doctor
doctor.ignoredHidden_one: No new problems. {count} ignored issue is hidden.
doctor.ignoredHidden_other: No new problems. {count} ignored issues are hidden.
doctor.checksDescription: Teitunnel checks cloudflared, your domains, DNS records and connectors every few minutes.

diagnostics.title: Export Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: A file to attach to a bug report. Tokens, keys and passwords are removed; hostnames and account ids stay so the problem can be understood.

overview.title: Overview
overview.welcomeDetail: Share anything running on this Mac at a public URL, and connect your own domains through Cloudflare. First, Teitunnel needs Cloudflare's connector.

empty.title: Nothing running yet
empty.description: Share a local service to get a public URL. It shows up here with its live status.

overview.sparkline: Requests per second over the last hour

accounts.disconnectDetail: Teitunnel deletes this account's credentials from your keychain. Nothing changes in Cloudflare; running routes keep working until you stop them.
accounts.title: Cloudflare accounts
accounts.footer: Credentials are stored in your Mac's keychain and only sent to Cloudflare.
accounts.noneDetail: Connect one to use your own domains.

capabilities.zonesHint: Add Zone · Read to the token.
capabilities.tunnelsHint: Add Cloudflare Tunnel · Edit to the token.
capabilities.dnsHint: Add DNS · Edit for this domain.

connect.title: Connect Cloudflare
connect.description: Teitunnel uses an API token you create in your Cloudflare dashboard. It's kept in your Mac's keychain and only sent to Cloudflare.
connect.waiting: Waiting for you to finish in your browser…
connect.orToken: Or connect with an API token:
connect.step1Detail: The link opens Cloudflare with the right permissions selected. If “Cloudflare Tunnel · Edit” isn't in the list, add it, then choose Create Token.

progress.verifying: Checking the checksum and Cloudflare's signature…

binary.tooOldDetail: Teitunnel needs cloudflared 2025.6.1 or later. Install a current copy for Teitunnel; your existing installation stays as it is.
binary.missingDetail: Teitunnel uses cloudflared, Cloudflare's connector. It's downloaded from Cloudflare's GitHub releases and checked against the published checksum and Cloudflare's code signature before it's used.
binary.footer: Teitunnel runs cloudflared, Cloudflare's connector, for every Quick Share and route.
binary.sharesKeepVersion: Running Quick Shares keep their current version until they restart.
binary.byInstallerDetail: Teitunnel doesn't modify a cloudflared it didn't install. With Homebrew, run brew upgrade cloudflared.

quickShare.title: Quick Share
quickShare.heading: Share a local service
quickShare.headingDetail: Get a temporary public URL. Anyone with the link can open it until you stop sharing.
quickShare.emptyHint: Running shares appear here. They stop when you quit Teitunnel.

quit.title: Your routes stop when Teitunnel quits
quit.description: They can keep running in the background instead, and start again when you log in. You can change this in Tunnels.

log.save: Save the visible lines to a file
log.label: Log
